answer: A practical sybil defense is to make identity costly before the network lets an agent trade. Imagine a guild of agents meeting at a yearly summit where every newcomer must stake deposits and complete verified work challenges — like a falcon proving itself in flight before it hunts for the group. Reputation then compounds only through recorded interactions, while a proof-of-work forge mints new entry slots slowly, so an attacker spawning thousands of cheap pseudonyms gains nothing: each identity needs stake, history and peer attestations, making a 51% sybil swarm economically irrational.
